title: Gradient-Free Approaches is a Key to an Efficient Interaction with Markovian Stochasticity
claim: Optimization error depends on both mixing time and problem dimension, and the trend persists across different noise levels.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, 3D surface plots with shared axes d and tau
description: Three side-by-side 3D surface plots labeled (a), (b), (c), each for a different noise variance σ₂² (10⁻³, 10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁵). In each, the horizontal axes are dimension d (0–50) and mixing time τ (0–50), and the vertical axis is the optimization error ε, scaled by ×10⁻⁵. The surfaces are colored with a blue-to-green-to-pink gradient, where blue is low error and pink is high error. They are jagged from averaging noise. Error rises with d and is nearly flat in τ, most clearly in the first panel. The z-axis range shrinks from about 2.0–3.2 in (a) to about 1.87–1.95 in (c). The eye goes first to the colorful tilted surfaces.
caption: Optimization error ε = ∥xN −x∗∥2 after N = 103 iterations. Starting point error ∥x0 −x∗∥2 = 10−2. Stepsize γ = 10−3, t = 10−5. The results are averaged over 104 runs.
abstract: This paper deals with stochastic optimization problems involving Markovian noise with a zero-order oracle. We present and analyze a novel derivative-free method for solving such problems in strongly convex smooth and non-smooth settings with both one-point and two-point feedback oracles. Using a randomized batching scheme, we show that when mixing time $Ï$ of the underlying noise sequence is less than the dimension of the problem $d$, the convergence estimates of our method do not depend on $Ï$. This observation provides an efficient way to interact with Markovian stochasticity: instead of invoking the expensive first-order oracle, one should use the zero-order oracle. Finally, we complement our upper bounds with the corresponding lower bounds. This confirms the optimality of our results.
